posts.name: scifantasy
posts.cooked:
I called James Hong as soon as they said Zhu Long. Because yes, once you've played Lo Pan you are the go-to for every other "Not Fu Manchu, Really" role. I know, it's a bit of Central Casting stereotyping; but Zhu Long (like most other NFMRs) exists as a post-hoc metacommentary on that exact role anyway...and I think I've disappeared in a Klein Bottle of metacommentary now.

Keith David is inspired casting for OblivAeon.

One aspect of voice casting as opposed to live-action casting is that it is a different skillset, and there are reasons that there are "regulars" in that industry too, who are distinct. (The How Stuff Works network of podcasts did a dozen episodes this past summer about animation, called "Drawn"; their episode on voice acting was fascinating.) Tara Strong, Maurice LaMarche, Rob Paulsen..there are reasons their names keep popping up. So yeah, if we assume the Metaverse that has Sentinel Comics as the major comis industry, then their names would show up there as well. (Whoops, there's that Klein Bottle again.)

posts.name: The Girl With No Name
posts.cooked:
Jeffrey Combs as Writhe?

...Perfect.

I figured this episode was going to be a total snooze for me, since I don’t know ANYBODY in the voice-acting world, beyond really famous people like Keith David. But then I figured out an angle that would work for me to push, and I’m gonna make a project of it over coming weeks as I get time. I don’t know any modern VAs, so instead I’ll use classic VAs from the Golden Age of Radio, which I’m extremely familiar with. Since most people won’t know these mostly long dead individuals, I’ll include a YouTube clip with each one so you can hear them saying something that I can directly imagine them saying in-character. Obviously, it’ll take some time to collect almost 100 samples, so watch this space.

To start us off, here’s Peggy Webber as Nightmist:
